Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
mark.wilkin wrote:
>
> I was just wonder does anyone actually use catiff in their decks as most
> of the decks I see here never touch them.
> Are they actually any good at all.

It really depends on (a) what kind of deck you're playing and (b) how
bad the disad. on the particular Caitiff/Pander is.

For example, Hasina Kesi is rather mighty, since she's got Potence. She
can Bum's Rush, play Torn Signpost, Immortal Grapple, ... all the good
combat cards you'd want her to, and then she can Disarm and diablerize
you. Her disadvantage simply makes her cost 2 (like KoKo or Lupo), and
you just make sure she doesn't go to torpor again.

A vampire like Navar McCracken is just plain bad. He's only got
Animalism, which is really good for blocking people (which he can't do),
and really good in combination with other disciplines (which he doesn't
have). Vliam Andor is 10 times better (but still pretty bad himself).

Someone like Igo the Hungry is kind of middle of the road. For example,
in my Deep Space Bled For Nine deck (a Pre/Obf weenie bleed deck), Igo
is perfect, since he's a 1 with presence. His disadvantage is kind of
minor, as long as you have Hunting Grounds or some other way to prevent
him from having to hunt.

So, you see, it really varies, though some of the Caitiff/Pander are
really bad, and some are exceptionally good (I didn't even mention Jimmy
Dunn).

James

Messages.Author: Richard D. Zopf
Messages.Body:
aa4...@zen.sunderland.ac.uk (mark.wilkin) wrote:

>I was just wonder does anyone actually use catiff in their decks as most
>of the decks I see here never touch them.

>Are they actually any good at all. I usually stick either Nik or smudge
>the ignored in just to give smudge fame or try and get Nik that +1 hamd
>damage. It's never going to happen but its something to aim for :-)

Caitiff need a deck built around them that allows for their weaknesses
(low capacity, often easily torpored, etc.). When used as
flavor/support for favorite decks, they often end up as just a
punching dummy for whomever comes at you.
When used as a deck concept unto themselves, they can be devastating.
When you think about it, you get all the abilities of any other basic
vampire, but for a single pool. Caitiff can bleed for one, hunt,
diablerize, equip, etc., and you haven't cashed out even a minor
fraction of your pool.
Extend this to a crypt that includes all the one capacities (including
Pander), and you have 14 vampires (although most people would leave
out Uriah Winter). Build a deck heavy on the Parthenon, Effective
Managements, Info Highway, and Computer Hackings, and you'll have 14
seperate bleed actions per turn at the expense of 14-18 pool. If
you're worried about losing too many to combat, include some Leather
Jackets. If the pool loss bothers you, Tribute to the Master (so you
hunt for a turn...you've just gained 14 pool). Stick to free
equipment, and the basics that every Vampire gets, and you have a
pretty intimidating deck...
Yeah, Caitiff can be good, even Nik...

Regards,

Mark Wilkin wrote:
"I was just wonder does anyone actually use catiff in their decks as most of
the decks I see here never touch them.
Are they actually any good at all. I usually stick either Nik or smudge the
ignored in just to give smudge fame or try and get Nik that +1 hamd damage.
It's never going to happen but its something to aim for :-)"

Nah. People use the Caitif all the time. Most deck archtypes have a Caitif or
two that can easily fit in, like incredibly handy Hasina Kessi in a Potence
Rush deck or Nik in a Brujah deck. More often than that, however, the Caitif
show up in weenie based decks that rely on all small vampires. Very strong and
fast Presence based bleed decks use plenty of Caitif (as there are a good
supply with Pre). The archtypical "wennie vote" deck tends to use all Caitif
with complete disregard to their disciplines, as does some sort of inhuman wave
bleed deck, that consists of nothing but Caitif, Effective Management, Info
Highway, Misdirection, and Computer Hacking.
